newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel in Bezeq talks with Cable & Wireless.
newsitem.headline: Israel in Bezeq talks with Cable & Wireless.

text.p: Israel's communications minister said she held her first talks with the chief executive of Cable & Wireless Plc on privatising Bezeq Israel Telecom, in which the British company has a 10 percent stake.

Limor Livnat told Israel Television no decisions were taken at the three-hour meeting with Cable & Wireless chief executive Richard Brown. She said further talks would be held late next week in London.

"We had negotiations today because I thought we should try to open a clean slate and reach agreements and understandings with them that will enable us to proceed together towards a public offering (of Bezeq)," Livnat said.

"We could proceed with an offering without them but of course, this would make it very difficult," she said, describing as "excellent" her first meeting with Brown since the Likud government took office in June pledging to push privatisation.

Israel's former Labour government and Cable & Wireless had failed to reach an agreement on future purchases of Bezeq by the British firm and the possibility of it becoming a strategic partner in Israel's main telecommunications company.

Earlier this month, Cable & Wireless asked Israeli privatisation authorities for permission to increase its Bezeq stake to 21 percent. Livnat was not asked about the request in the television interview.

"We will offer Bezeq shares on the global market, apparently through offerings in the United States and London and perhaps on the Israeli market. All the possibilities are being investigated right now," Livnat said in the television interview.

"It will not happen before the second half of 1997 because there are (already) tremendous offerings of telecommunications companies on the world markets, which, by the way, have been very successful," she said.

Last month, Livnat said she had hoped to proceed with a global offering of 24 percent of Bezeq later this year. Israeli government officials said on Wednesday that Bezeq is slated for further privatisation only next year.
She told the television that the government eventually wanted to divest itself entirely of Bezeq.
"We still haven't decided if this will be through the sale of a controlling stake or by continuing share offerings," Livnat said.
